open_points.subject: direct service access and personal-data boundary
open_points.text: “Owner … is the only reader of personal data”; “values of class `personal_data` reach an agent only as digest and class”; but “An agent's own access to a service … is granted by that service and the owner outside the kernel”
open_points.question: Are the statements that only the owner reads personal data and that agents receive only digests limited to data returned through the kernel, so an agent may receive personal data directly from a service?
options: Limit both statements explicitly to the kernel surface
Prohibit personal-data disclosure through agents' direct service access
Define a separate restriction for direct access
open_points.default_guess: Limit both statements to the kernel surface, matching the new exclusion.

open_points.subject: installation administrator
open_points.text: “tokens configured in the installation”; “service credentials and tokens live in the installation's protected configuration”; “the installation names”
open_points.question: Who may create and change the owner token, agent-token list, credentials, listener address, manifest and selected service instances, and is that actor the owner or a separate trusted operator?
options: The owner is the installation administrator
A separate trusted operator exists
Configuration is provisioned by an unnamed external platform
open_points.default_guess: Treat the owner as the installation administrator.

open_points.subject: owner authentication
open_points.text: “Reaches the kernel through the agent channel with the owner's token.”
open_points.question: Where is the owner token configured, how is it distinguished from agent tokens, when do changes or revocation take effect, and what observable failure does a missing or invalid token produce?
options: Manage it alongside agent tokens with the same reload and comparison rules
Use authentication supplied by the reverse proxy
Define separate owner-token lifecycle rules
open_points.default_guess: Manage it in protected installation configuration and validate it on every request.

open_points.subject: authentication failures
open_points.text: “Each action names its observable output and its failure.”
open_points.question: What does the surface return when authentication fails or the authenticated actor is not allowed to perform the requested action?
options: One authentication/authorization refusal with a reason
Distinct unauthenticated and forbidden failures
Let the proxy reject authentication before the kernel
open_points.default_guess: Return distinct unauthenticated and forbidden refusals without creating domain records.

open_points.subject: author permission scope
open_points.text: “the token says whether the agent may author”; function and trial actions require “agent with author right”, while “propose an operation binding” and “compose and prove a flow” name any agent
open_points.question: Does `may-author` govern only function implementations and trial corpora, or also flow composition and binding proposals?
options: It governs every persistent authoring action
It governs only functions and trial corpora
Use separate permissions for functions, flows and bindings
open_points.default_guess: Require `may-author` for every action that creates persistent authored definitions.

open_points.subject: agent inspection context
open_points.text: “inspect functions, flows, runs, bindings, approvals, standing grants and effect attempts”; “For repair an agent receives one contract, its current implementation and that slot's recent traces and trial evidence; for composition, contracts, bindings and not implementation bodies.”
open_points.question: How does the kernel know whether an inspection is for repair or composition, and exactly which implementation bodies, traces and trial evidence may an agent inspect?
options: Expose separate repair and composition inspection actions
Require an explicit inspection purpose and slot
Allow all agents to inspect all implementation bodies
open_points.default_guess: Expose distinct repair and composition views, with repair scoped to one slot.

open_points.subject: new contract version becoming current
open_points.text: “the first contract of a new slot name creates the slot”; “an earlier implementation of the slot's current contract version”
open_points.question: When a later contract version is authored, does it automatically become the slot's current contract version, who may make that transition, and what happens to the previous activation?
options: Authoring makes the new contract version current and leaves it inactive until admission
Add an explicit contract-version activation action
Keep every contract version independently addressable with no single current version
open_points.default_guess: Authoring makes the new contract version current, with no active implementation until one is admitted.

open_points.subject: implementation submission and admission trigger
open_points.text: “author a function contract or implementation”; “try an implementation”; “admit and activate — kernel, when an implementation is submitted”
open_points.question: What action constitutes submitting an implementation for admission, and is it distinct from authoring or trying it?
options: Authoring automatically submits it to whole-corpus admission
Trying the whole corpus submits it when all cases pass
Add an explicit submit-for-admission action
open_points.default_guess: Add an explicit submit-for-admission action after optional trials.

open_points.subject: trial execution scope
open_points.text: “try an implementation — trial evidence per case”
open_points.question: Does a try execute one selected case, selected cases, or the entire active corpus, and may an agent without `may-author` supply transient code to try?
options: Try one named existing implementation against the whole corpus
Try selected cases of an existing implementation
Permit transient code trials without persisting an implementation
open_points.default_guess: Try a persisted implementation against the whole active corpus; author rights are required to create it.

open_points.subject: trial-case oracle
open_points.text: “add a trial case”; “the case every later implementation must pass”
open_points.question: What constitutes a passing trial case—expected output, expected failure, predicates, or only successful contract conformance—and who supplies or approves that oracle?
options: A case contains inputs and exact expected outputs
A case requires only successful schema-conforming execution
A case contains an explicit expected verdict or output matcher
open_points.default_guess: Store inputs plus exact expected outputs and require the author to supply them.

open_points.subject: captured failure oracle
open_points.text: “capture a failed execution into the trial corpus … the trial case every later implementation must pass”
open_points.question: Because a failed execution may have no correct output, how is the expected result for the captured regression case obtained?
options: The capturing actor supplies the expected output
Capture only the inputs and require later schema-valid success
Allow capture only after a successful corrected execution establishes the output
open_points.default_guess: Capture the inputs and require the capturing actor to provide an expected output.

open_points.subject: manual file fixtures
open_points.text: “add a trial case”; “The only files the kernel keeps beyond a run are the file fixtures of trial cases”; but “a caller never hands the kernel a file”
open_points.question: How can a file fixture be added to a trial case when callers cannot provide files to the kernel?
options: File fixtures can only be captured from failed runs
Allow a dedicated fixture-upload action
Allow a case to reference a file held by a service
open_points.default_guess: Permit file fixtures only through capture from an unreleased failed run.

open_points.subject: function execution interface
open_points.text: “A function node runs one admitted implementation of one contract: declared input in, declared output out”
open_points.question: What Python entry point and value/file representation connect contract ports to implementation code, and how does code report a normal result versus a function failure?
options: A fixed callable receiving and returning typed dictionaries
One generated callable signature per contract
A process protocol over serialized input and output
open_points.default_guess: Use a fixed callable receiving a port-name dictionary and returning a port-name dictionary.

open_points.subject: Python runtime determinism
open_points.text: “Functions are written in Python only”; “the Python standard library only”; “Admission is a deterministic verdict”
open_points.question: Which Python implementation/version, enabled standard-library modules and runtime environment are pinned so that admission and later real execution have the same deterministic behavior?
options: Pin one exact Python runtime and an allowed-module list
Support an installation-selected compatible Python version
Treat all standard-library modules as allowed and rely only on sandbox controls
open_points.default_guess: Pin an exact Python runtime and explicitly block clock, randomness, networking, process and unrestricted filesystem modules.

open_points.subject: sandbox authority and limits
open_points.text: “runs in a disposable isolated environment with bounded time, memory, output and processes”; contracts declare “resource bounds”
open_points.question: What trusted component enforces sandbox isolation, what resource dimensions and installation maxima exist, and what happens when a contract requests bounds above those maxima?
options: An in-process sandbox with installation caps
A trusted external container/process sandbox with installation caps
Contract authors may choose any finite bounds
open_points.default_guess: Use a trusted external sandbox with installation-wide maxima and refuse contracts exceeding them.

open_points.subject: value-schema system
open_points.text: “Every port carries a value schema. An edge is valid when both ports carry the same schema.”
open_points.question: What schema language and canonical equality rule define when two port schemas are the same, including collections, records, optional values and file ports?
options: Canonical JSON Schema equality
A closed kernel-native type algebra
Byte-for-byte equality of stored schema documents
open_points.default_guess: Use a closed kernel-native type algebra with canonical serialization.

open_points.subject: effect-class authority
open_points.text: “Effect classes are `read`, `draft-write`, `state-transition`, `external-effect`, `destructive`.”
open_points.question: Which record declares an operation node's effect class, who is trusted to assign it, and what check prevents an effectful service operation from being bound as `read`?
options: The signed/trusted platform manifest declares it
The proposed binding declares it and the owner accepts it
The flow author assigns it per node
open_points.default_guess: Require the platform manifest's operation record to declare it and include it in the pinned digest.

open_points.subject: idempotency-key contract
open_points.text: “The kernel supplies the declared idempotency key”
open_points.question: Where does an operation declare whether and how the key is inserted into its HTTP request, which classes require support, and what happens when an operation cannot accept one?
options: The manifest operation declares a header or body location
Use one fixed HTTP header for all services
Require keys only for approval-stopped classes
open_points.default_guess: Put the key location and support requirement in the pinned manifest operation record for every non-read operation.

open_points.subject: manifest trust and refresh
open_points.text: “Microservices — known only as records of the platform manifest”; “the token list again whenever it has changed”
open_points.question: Who supplies and may modify the manifest, whether the kernel trusts it as control data, how changes are detected, and what observable failure follows an unavailable or malformed manifest are unstated.
options: Read a trusted local manifest on every relevant request
Load and validate a trusted manifest at startup and explicitly reload it
Fetch it from a trusted platform service
open_points.default_guess: Treat a validated local manifest as trusted control data and reload it when its content changes.

open_points.subject: service transport trust
open_points.text: “Outbound, the kernel calls microservices over their HTTP APIs.”
open_points.question: What authenticates service identity and protects credentials, personal data and business-confidential values in transit—HTTPS with certificate validation, a trusted private network, or something else?
options: Require HTTPS and certificate validation
Permit plain HTTP only on a separately trusted network
Leave transport security to each manifest entry
open_points.default_guess: Require HTTPS with certificate validation for non-loopback service endpoints.

open_points.subject: operation invocation outcomes
open_points.text: “pending when a service is unreachable or an outcome unknown”; “their answers are untrusted data until validated at the port”
open_points.question: How are connection failure, timeout before send, timeout after possible send, HTTP error, oversized response and schema-invalid response classified as `pending`, `outcome_unknown` or node failure for each effect class?
options: Define outcome rules from request transmission state and effect class
Treat every transport failure as unreachable
Treat every failure after dispatch as outcome unknown
open_points.default_guess: Use transmission state: failure before possible send is unreachable, uncertainty after a non-read send is outcome unknown, and validated HTTP/application errors are node failures.

open_points.subject: unknown outcomes for read and draft operations
open_points.text: “Effect classes are `read`, `draft-write`, `state-transition`, `external-effect`, `destructive`”; “never repeats an effect without a fresh approval”; “a resend needs a fresh approval, as for every class”
open_points.question: Do outcome-unknown resolution and fresh-approval-on-resend apply to `read` operations as well as every write class, and does a repeated `draft-write` require approval despite not requiring approval initially?
options: Apply them to every class including reads
Apply them to every non-read class
Apply them only to approval-stopped classes plus draft-write
open_points.default_guess: Apply unknown-outcome resolution and fresh approval to every non-read operation, but retry reads without approval.

open_points.subject: standing-grant eligibility
open_points.text: “each `state-transition`, `external-effect` and `destructive` node stops … unless … a standing approval”; but the grant action refuses only “a `destructive` node”
open_points.question: May the owner create meaningless standing grants for `read` and `draft-write` nodes, or are grants valid only for `state-transition` and `external-effect` nodes?
options: Only state-transition and external-effect nodes may receive grants
Every non-destructive node may receive a grant
Draft-write grants have a separately defined meaning
open_points.default_guess: Allow grants only for state-transition and external-effect nodes.

open_points.subject: run inputs and disclosure classes
open_points.text: “run a flow — owner, agent”; “A flow's own inputs and outputs are values, never files”; “Every value carries `open`, `business_confidential` or `personal_data`.”
open_points.question: What inputs does the run action accept, who assigns or verifies each input's schema and disclosure class, and what failure is returned for a missing, extra, invalid or falsely classified value?
options: The active flow declares input schemas/classes and the caller supplies matching values
The caller supplies both values and trusted class labels
Flows have no caller inputs and acquire all data through operation nodes
open_points.default_guess: Have each flow version declare input schemas and maximum classes, validate supplied values, and prevent callers from lowering a value's established class.

open_points.subject: zero-input function classification
open_points.text: “a function's output takes the highest class its execution received”
open_points.question: What disclosure class is assigned to output from a function with no inputs, and can a function contract declare a higher fixed output class?
options: Zero-input output is `open`
Every function output declares a minimum class
Prohibit zero-input functions
open_points.default_guess: Use `open` for zero-input output and allow a contract-declared minimum class.

open_points.subject: approval result when sending fails
open_points.text: “approve or refuse an effect — … the effect runs on the exact input shown”; “An approval whose effect was never sent (the service was unreachable) stays valid on resume”
open_points.question: What observable result does approval return when the service is unreachable, the outcome becomes unknown, or the service returns a failing or invalid response?
options: Return the updated run and attempt status
Return only the recorded approval and let inspection reveal execution state
Keep the approval call open until a terminal node result
open_points.default_guess: Return the recorded approval plus the resulting run and effect-attempt status.

open_points.subject: resolution as applied without an output
open_points.text: “the effect is recorded applied, or not applied; the run continues”
open_points.question: If an operation resolved as `applied` has output ports but no validated response was received, what values feed its dependent nodes?
options: Resolution must include owner-supplied validated outputs
Such a node's dependants fail or are skipped
Only outputless operations may be resolved as applied
open_points.default_guess: Require the owner to supply schema-valid outputs when downstream nodes need them.

open_points.subject: cancellation and in-flight sends
open_points.text: “cancel a run — the run ends `cancelled`; nothing further is sent”
open_points.question: Can a run be cancelled while an HTTP operation is in flight, and if so how is the possibly applied outcome recorded and prevented from being mistaken for a clean cancellation?
options: Cancellation waits for any in-flight call to settle
Cancellation records an unknown outcome for an in-flight non-read send
Runs cannot be cancelled while an operation call is in flight
open_points.default_guess: Record an in-flight non-read send as outcome unknown and do not label the run cleanly cancelled until it is resolved.

open_points.subject: run completion after partial failure
open_points.text: “a failed node stops its dependants”
open_points.question: After one node fails, do independent branches continue, and exactly when does the run become `failed` and expose its final outputs?
options: Continue independent branches, then end failed
Stop scheduling every remaining node immediately
Make branch-failure policy part of the flow
open_points.default_guess: Continue already eligible independent branches, then end the run `failed`.

open_points.subject: mapped and skipped trace records
open_points.text: “Every node execution writes one immutable trace record”; “an execution that … was skipped … is refused”
open_points.question: Does each mapped item create its own execution and trace record, and does a guard-skipped node create a trace record even though it did not execute?
options: One trace per mapped invocation and one skipped record per skipped invocation
One aggregate trace per graph node
Only actual executions produce traces
open_points.default_guess: Create one trace per concrete mapped invocation and explicit skipped trace records.

open_points.subject: reading traces failure
open_points.text: “read a trace | owner, agent | trace records | —”
open_points.question: What happens for an unknown run or trace reference, an invalid filter or an unauthorized request, despite the statement that every action names a failure?
options: Return an empty collection for no matches and refuse malformed or unknown direct references
Refuse every unknown reference
Treat trace reading as infallible apart from authentication
open_points.default_guess: Return empty results for searches, but refuse unknown direct references and invalid filters.

open_points.subject: owner retrieval of stored values
open_points.text: “The owner receives every value”; traces contain “input and output by digest”; inspection returns a “typed description”
open_points.question: Which action lets the owner retrieve a stored non-file value identified only by a trace digest, and what happens if the value or digest is unknown?
options: Trace reading dereferences values for the owner
Inspection has a get-value-by-digest form
Run inspection always embeds all retained values
open_points.default_guess: Add a get-value-by-digest form to inspection, with personal values available only to the owner.

open_points.subject: secret-echo withholding outcome
open_points.text: “A service's own answer body that echoes one verbatim is withheld from everyone … and never used as an output”
open_points.question: When a response body contains a configured secret verbatim, does the node fail, become pending, return a special withheld value, or continue without an output, and what trace information is recorded?
options: Fail the node with a secret-echo refusal and record no body
Return a typed withheld marker
Treat it as an invalid service response
open_points.default_guess: Fail the node with a distinct secret-echo reason while storing neither the body nor its digest.

open_points.subject: persistent-store confidentiality
open_points.text: “The owner receives every value”; “Values … are kept for as long as the kernel keeps its traces”; “Backup and restore … are an operational procedure outside the kernel.”
open_points.question: Who can read the kernel store and its backups, and what protects indefinitely retained personal and confidential values from installation operators or filesystem readers?
options: The owner is also the only trusted store operator
A separate operator is trusted with ciphertext only
The kernel encrypts sensitive values with an owner-controlled key
open_points.default_guess: Encrypt sensitive stored values and backups with an owner-controlled installation key.

open_points.subject: fixed MCP surface versus primary actions
open_points.text: “one fixed set of typed operations over `mcp`: inspect, author, try, run, resume, read traces, and the owner's approve, accept, activate, grant, revoke, resolve and cancel”
open_points.question: Which MCP operations implement add trial case, capture failure, release failed run, rollback, propose binding, compose/prove flow and agent activation of read-only flows, all of which are primary actions but are absent or described as owner-only in the fixed list?
options: Define each as a separate fixed MCP operation
Specify exact subcommands under `author`, `inspect` and `activate`
Revise the primary-action list to match the stated surface
open_points.default_guess: Expose separate typed operations for materially different actions and permit agent activation only for proven read-only versions.

open_points.subject: effectful-flow rehearsal transfer
open_points.text: “Effectful flows are rehearsed on an installation of disposable rigs.”
open_points.question: How does a flow, its contracts, implementations, trial evidence and bindings move from the disposable-rig installation to the target installation, given that no export, import or promotion action exists?
options: Recreate all records independently through existing authoring actions
Add signed export/import or promotion actions
Treat rehearsal as an external test with no artifact transfer
open_points.default_guess: Treat rehearsal as external and recreate immutable content-addressed artifacts through the normal actions on the target installation.
